content.thinking:
I'm setting up the JSON spec with the ordered list of outcomes and the SOP reference for that order. Next I'm working through the unknowns rule and how the "incomplete" outcome should be justified, while checking how the quoted text has to match the cited section.

I'm checking whether "incomplete" can be justified from the 2.2 unknowns text by pairing it with the Section 1 definition, and I'm weighing whether the identified individuals for the collection rule should be only the control person and 25%+ owners, or also those the agent lists.

I'm checking whether excluded entities drop out of both the control person and owner requirements, since 3.1 and 3.2 seem to say so. For nonprofits, 3.3 only asks for owners when they aren't excluded or nonprofit, so I'm weighing a condition that treats the control person and 25%+ owners differently.

I'm settling on the identified individuals as the control person and anyone owning 25% or more, leaving out certified_pct since the SOP doesn't mention certification. For excluded entities no identified individuals are needed, and a missing control person for a non-excluded entity goes to request_docs rather than an empty list.

I'm settling on the source for the collection rule, weighing whether the nonprofit exception and the excluded-entity exception should be attached to the owner threshold or handled separately, and deciding the single section citation has to be 3.3 since that's where the owner requirement lives.

I'm going back over the excluded-owners collection and realizing it doesn't need a counts_when condition at all, since an empty list sums to zero. I'll leave that entry out rather than add a rule that the SOP doesn't call for.

I'm weighing how the unaccounted share affects completeness: if the shares not tied to a known person amount to 25% or more, an unidentified person could hold that much, so ownership can't be called complete.

I'm checking whether an unidentified person could reach 25% by combining an identified person's known share with the unaccounted share, not just the unaccounted share on its own. The literal reading seems to point that way, but the rule's "some" only looks at people who meet the identification condition, so I'll have to work out how to bring the unaccounted share into the calculation.

Checking whether the share held through an excluded entity can still hide an unidentified person: if that entity holds less than 25%, the people behind it might still reach the threshold once their shares are combined with what they hold directly.

I'm working out the open share as the unaccounted share plus any excluded-owner share under 25%, since those could still belong to an unidentified person. That gives a computed sum for the open share, and the excluded-owner part is limited to holdings below the threshold.

I'm checking whether the open share should also include the part held through excluded entities under 25%, since individuals behind those could still reach the threshold. I'm also noticing a gap: a known person holding a small share could combine it with the unaccounted share to reach 25%, and the rule's "some" can't see people who aren't identified, so I'll have to work around that.

I'm checking whether the open share rule needs a fact for the largest known share held by someone who isn't identified, since a person below 25% could still reach the threshold once combined with the unaccounted share. The rule's "some" can't see unidentified people, so that value has to come in as a separate input.

I'm checking the rule for owners who aren't listed by the agent, since 3.3 asks to identify every individual at 25% or more. I'm weighing whether an unlisted owner should make ownership incomplete, or whether the unaccounted share already covers that case.

I'm moving on to the control person rule, which requires a request for documents when none is identified for a non-excluded entity. Then I'm checking the identity verification step, where any unverified individual means requesting documents. Last, the registry age check: a registry record of 12 months or more means documents are needed, and an 11-month-29-day record still counts as under the limit.

Now I'm going through the sanctions and PEP rules, checking which entity and people checks escalate or decline, and starting on the adverse media rule.

I'm working through the sanctions-related and adverse media rules, deciding that adverse media on the entity or an identified individual escalates only when it is material. I'm also noting that the industry rules conflict: the MSB escalation in 5.2 seems to contradict the licensed-MSB approval in 5.3, so I'll have to decide how to handle that.

I'm weighing whether approve needs its own rule, since the order ends with it and no rule so far covers the case where nothing else applies. I'm also looking at how the MSB escalation in 5.2 sits against the licensed-MSB approval in 5.3.

I'm weighing whether an approve rule with an always-true condition is needed as the fallback, since the order ends with approve and nothing so far covers the case where no other rule applies. I'm also noting that the 5.3 approve rule can never take effect because the 5.2 escalation for MSBs already overrides it.

I'm settling on an approve rule that always applies, since the order ends with approve and this makes it the fallback. The 5.3 licensed-MSB approval can't take effect anyway, because the 5.2 escalation for MSBs already overrides it.

I'm weighing whether to keep a default approve rule with an always-true condition, since approve is last in the order and nothing else may catch the no-rule case. The 5.3 licensed-MSB approval would be subsumed by it anyway, so I'm leaning toward including it.

I'm settling on a catch-all approve rule that always applies, since approve comes last in the order. I'm also noting the industry map I'm building: the prohibited categories and the MSB and crypto groupings, with the exact SOP wording used as keys.

I'm weighing whether an industry word with no mapping should count as unknown, since that would make ordinary businesses incomplete under the industry rules. The SOP lists no normal industries, so I'm checking what 2.2 says about a required fact that can't be determined.

I'm mapping the industry words now, starting with the normal categories like software, retail and consulting so that ordinary businesses aren't left unknown. I'm also wondering whether a separate entry is needed for licensed money services businesses, since they sit apart from the plain MSB wording.

I'm working through the sanctions rules now: a sanctioned country on the entity or a sanctioned residence means decline, while a high-risk jurisdiction escalates, with decline taking precedence for countries on both lists. An unknown country or residence would leave the outcome incomplete.

I'm turning to the 3.3 ownership rule, which needs the largest share held by someone who isn't identified, since a person below 25% could still reach the threshold once the unaccounted share is added. I'm also starting the 4.4 search-recording requirement, covering the terms that have to be logged.

I'm checking the 3.3 ownership rule, which needs the largest share held by a person who isn't identified, since someone below 25% could still reach the threshold once the unaccounted share is added. I'm also noting the 4.4 search-recording requirement as a procedural note rather than an outcome.

I'm checking the unknowns wording, where a fact not yet established counts as unknown rather than false and blocks approval, and I'm seeing how that leads to the incomplete outcome. I'm also noting that the excluded-entity rules and the control person fallback still stand, and that a listed 10% owner who is a PEP would not escalate under the SOP as written.

I'm working out the default approve rule and the licensed-MSB approval, and noting that the identified-individuals collection will be tied to the 3.3 owner threshold, with the 3.1 and 3.2 control-person rules shaping it.

I'm finishing the note on the control person rule and the 3.2 wording for non-excluded entities, then tying the nonprofit case in 3.3 to the excluded-entity sentence before turning to the industry map.

unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

people.unknown_when_empty: who the identified individuals are (the control person and every individual owning 25% or more)
people.text: Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly.

computed.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share. If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.
A confirmed sanctions match on the entity or any identified individual: decline.
A potential sanctions match that has not been cleared: escalate.
A politically exposed person among the identified individuals: escalate.

Adverse media on the entity or any identified individual: escalate. Adverse media counts only if it is material. A report counts only if it matches the name and at least one other identifier (age, location or role), and comes from a court record, a regulator or an established news outlet, or from two independent other sources.
Prohibited industries (marijuana-related business, adult content, unlicensed money transmission): decline.
Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
Licensed money services businesses whose state licence has been verified may be approved.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country: decline.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a FATF high-risk or increased-monitoring jurisdiction: escalate.
all requirements below are met and no risk factor applies.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Approve is the fallback when no other rule applies. Incomplete is the outcome for unknowns, through 2.2.
Sets `order`: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve.
Sets `unknowns`. A rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to incomplete (Section 1: 'a required fact has not been established yet').

No outcome of its own. It sets the people list's empty_ok_when: an excluded entity needs no identified individuals. It is also the source of the 'not excluded' conditions in counts_when and in rules bo-control-person-missing and bo-ownership-incomplete.
Also makes the control person (of a non-excluded entity) an identified individual in the people list's counts_when.

It sets the 25% owner part of counts_when (not for excluded entities or nonprofits). It also defines the computed open_share_pct: unaccounted_pct plus the shares held through excluded entities that own less than 25%.
The SOP doesn't say whose match. This rule applies it to the entity and to identified individuals, as in 4.1.

The materiality and source bar is built into the adverse_media facts. 'Record every search: the terms, the date and the sources reviewed.' is a working instruction with no outcome, so no rule comes from it.
The listed industries are mapped to 'prohibited' in maps.industry.
This conflicts with 5.3. A licensed, verified MSB still escalates under 5.2, which ranks above approve. Left as written.
'May be approved' is translated as an approve rule. Escalate from 5.2 always overrides it, so it never decides a case.
IR, KP and SY are also on the sanctioned list, so 6.1's decline wins for them.

needs.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown.
needs.fact: This sentence needs the largest known share held by any person who is not an identified individual (below 25%). Such a person could reach 25% when the open share is added to what they already hold. `some` only sees identified individuals, and unaccounted_pct alone treats the open share as if an unidentified person held nothing else. So none of the given facts can test whether, for example, a known 15% owner plus 12% unaccounted could own 25% or more.
